title: Evenings in Zhangjiajie - what to do
text: The park closes at sunset but the city wakes up. Watch the Tianmen Fox Fairy show (from 228 yuan), wander Wulingyuan's night market (food from 50 yuan), relax in hot springs (100-200 yuan), enjoy a Chinese foot massage (60-120 yuan per hour) or sing at a KTV karaoke.

title: Chinese holidays - when NOT to travel
text: When 1.4 billion people take holidays at once, Zhangjiajie becomes a nightmare. Avoid Golden Week (Oct 1-7) with 30,000+ daily visitors, Chinese New Year (Jan-Feb), Dragon Boat Festival (June), Mid-Autumn (Sept) and May Day. Best: weekdays in late October and November.

title: Tour or self-guided? A comparison
text: Self-guided: your own pace, 30-50% cheaper, full flexibility - but needs route planning and patience with the language. Organized tour: everything handled, guide tells stories - but rigid schedule and shopping stops. Compromise: hire a private guide for 300-500 yuan per day.

title: Zhangjiajie solo - is it worth it?
text: Absolutely yes. The park is perfect for solo travelers - extremely safe, well organized with buses, cable cars and signs, and hostels make finding trekking companions easy. Share group taxis to Grand Canyon, order small (xiao fen) portions at restaurants, and share your daily plan.

title: 10 mistakes tourists make in Zhangjiajie
text: Learn from others: trying to see it all in 1-2 days (need 4), arriving during Golden Week (30,000+ visitors daily), skipping a raincoat, wearing heels or sandals, too little water, feeding monkeys, no offline maps or translator, no cash, skipping Tianmen, no insurance.
